poster_title: Multi-Agent-as-Judge: Aligning LLM-Agent-Based Automated Evaluation with Multi-Dimensional Human Evaluation
authors: Jiaju Chen, Huimin Zeng, Ying Xu, Yuxuan Lu, Jing Huang, Bingsheng Yao, Xiaojie Wang, Jiri Gesi, Dakuo Wang

panels.headline: Traditional metrics insufficient for real-world NLP tasks
content: Collaborative human work requires multi-dimensional evaluation.
Domain-specific tasks need diverse perspectives for accurate assessment.
Traditional metrics (e.g., ROUGE-L) fail to capture real-world complexity.

panels.headline: Arbitrary and non-generalizable persona designs
content: Most frameworks are task-specific and hard to adapt.

panels.headline: Two-step design for constructing and deploying LLM agents
content: Extract diverse perspectives from text documents to construct agent personas.
Agents engage in in-group debates to refine initial judgments.
panels.figure_caption: The overview of MAJ-EVAL's two-step design: Step 1, MAJ-EVAL extracts stakeholders' diverse perspectives from the provided research papers and constructs corresponding personas for the LLM agents. Step 2, agents within the same stakeholder group engage in an in-group debate.

panels.headline: Improved alignment with human ratings
content: Conducted in educational and medical domains.
Tasks: question-answer generation for children's storybook reading and multi-document summarization of medical literature.
panels.figure_caption: Spearman's ρ (rank-based correlation) between evaluation methods and human ratings on StorySparkQA (left) and MSLR-COCHRANE (right). Higher values indicate stronger alignments with human judgments.

panels.headline: MAJ-EVAL outperforms traditional metrics and existing LLM methods
content: Demonstrated robustness and generalizability across domains.
Improved alignment with human ratings after in-group debate.
panels.figure_caption: Spearman correlations of MAJ-EVAL (Claude-3.7-Sonnet) stakeholder agents' initial and final scores with human judgments on StorySparkQA (left) and MSLR-COCHRANE (right). Dark blue bars higher than light blue bars indicate improved alignment with human ratings after in-group debate.

panels.headline: Promising approach for real-world NLG evaluation
content: MAJ-EVAL provides a systematic method for constructing and deploying human-aligned LLM agents.
Framework can adapt to different domain-specific evaluation tasks.
Future work: expanding to more domains and improving persona construction.
